doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: First paid gig at thirteen and the late-1990s swing revival
summary: He played a Pontiac coffee house with Band in a Box backing for $60 plus tips and enjoyed the swing revival while a hit with schoolmates.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well speaking of budgeting, do you remember how much money you made on your first paid gig?

Yes. I was just out of the seventh grade. I was 13. And I began playing at a coffee house in downtown Pontiac, Michigan. My band director knew the manager and he would accompany me down there. I didn’t have a band. So he had this computer program, Band in a Box you know, and you’d enter in the music and it would sound like a quartet playing behind you, so he cooked up about 30 or 40 tunes. And I would play there on weekends throughout the eighth grade. And yeah I remember I made $60 plus tips each time I played. And that was 1997 and it was really something.
That’s pretty good. Better than the $4 I made on my first gig.

Yeah it was a really neat period. Because the neat thing at that point was that was 1997 and if you remember swing music came back in fashion. There were a lot of swing bands out there that were making it in the charts again. You had Big Bad Voodoo Daddy, Brian Setzer, Royal Crown Revue. So all of a sudden I saw these young people getting into this music that I had been into for the prior few years. And you know my classmates didn’t quite get it, that I was into this older music, then all of a sudden they saw it in pop culture and I saw young folks that were into the same thing I was and that was really cool. Yeah.
I was going to say, were you a bit of a — have some notoriety in school because of your talents?

It was neat. You know I always say middle school is not generally the best period for most people, it’s just weird. Yeah let’s just get a bunch of people who have their hormones all over the place and put them in a building together. You know? It’s just a bad idea. But yeah I would play for the school, either play the clarinet or I’d play the guitar and do an Elvis Presley tune or something, and that seemed to help me make friends. And then my friends at school would come out and see me play wherever I was playing. So yeah, it was a wonderful thing.
